research_concepts: defense as a stable team trait
counter strategy and defensive best/avoid matchups
methodological_questions: is the team-level defensive H2-H1 effect reliable across seasons or split halves
how many team-seasons are needed to detect a stable defensive effect
does regression to the mean or selection on extreme team-seasons inflate apparent persistence
are H2-H1 change measures confounded by pace, rotation, garbage time, or score margin

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of a connector teammate-path quality metric (n=102 connectors): Pearson r=+0.215, Spearman rho=+0.242, Spearman-Brown about 0.355, ICC(player-season)=0.216 with 78.4% of variance within player. Recorded as too low to treat the metric as a stable scoutable trait.

Ranked playsheet validation over 10 series: full-rank Spearman null (rho=-0.0639, p=0.099717, n=665). Pairwise BEST vs AVOID difference was significant (Mann-Whitney U=5546.0, p=0.004018), but the record lists leakage, low measurement reliability, small sample and drift as limits.

Foul-trouble sequencing test: raw lag-1 effect of +0.204 was driven by free-throw share (41.8% treated vs 9.9% control). Apples-to-apples excluding FT gave +0.0486, CI [-0.0060, +0.0991], perm p=0.0655; no lag cleared CI, permutation and placebo checks.

Possession Control Index incremental R2 over ORtg (n=120 team-seasons): headline dR2=+0.139, but the record says the gain is leakage tracking DRtg (corr=+0.894). Offensive-control components added only +0.005 R2 beyond ORtg. The baseline omitted defense by construction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Split-half reliability test of a player-level derived on-off metric as a stable trait
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as low measurement reliability: split-half r=0.215, Spearman-Brown about 0.355, most variance within-player across halves (auto_limited_by LIM:low_measurement_reliability).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking play-type counter options against realized H2 scoring across 10 series
failed_approaches.why: Full-rank Spearman null; the only significant result was pairwise and the record notes leakage, small sample and low reliability; mechanism recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Foul-trouble lag effect including free throws
failed_approaches.why: Apparent effect was a free-throw composition artifact; the record says the effect vanished when FT possessions were removed (mechanism recorded as C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Incremental R2 of a derived control index over offensive rating for team-season outcomes
failed_approaches.why: Gain came from leakage correlated with the defensive outcome (corr=+0.894); baseline omitted defense by construction (recorded as C_artifact).

evidence_establishes: Analogous split-half reliability tests on derived per-unit metrics in this project have come out low (SF-APPS-085, r=0.215, Spearman-Brown about 0.355), which is a caution for a team-level H2-H1 trait.

Derived outcome-based constructions in this project have repeatedly produced artifacts (SF15, SF-APPS-068), so a defensive H2-H1 measure built from the same play-by-play risks leakage or composition effects.
No retrieved record tests whether a defense's opponent H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.
evidence_does_not_establish: Any estimate of reliability for team-level defensive H2-H1 change, since no retrieved record measures it.
Whether the 120 team-seasons in this data give enough power for a reliability claim.
Whether the analogous low reliabilities transfer to team-season defensive measures, which aggregate many more possessions than player-season connector metrics.
own_inferences: Team-season H2-H1 opponent change is a difference of two noisy half-game scoring rates, so its split-half reliability is likely low unless the metric is shrunk or aggregated over many more possessions.
With 120 team-seasons, a 95% CI on an ICC or cross-season correlation will likely be too wide to separate a trait from noise unless the true effect is large.
The question as posed (reliable trait) is a reliability claim, not a counter-strategy effect claim, so it may be answerable as a reliability test even if counter-strategy claims are not.
uncertainties: The retrieved records include no full defensive H2-H1 study, so the baseline reliability is unknown.
Whether 2025-26 regular season is complete enough for a holdout (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before) is not established here.
The data catalog and per-game possession counts were not examined in this step, so exposure per team-season is unknown.
Retrieved records were summarised from their listed fields; full texts were not read.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the question might look like a routine reliability test on 120 team-seasons. The retrieved records show low reliability on a closely analogous derived metric (SF-APPS-085) and repeated artifacts from derived, outcome-linked constructions (SF15, SF-APPS-068). These lower the expected power and raise leakage risk, so I moved to do_not_proceed as posed and proposed a narrower minimum viable test.

blocking_constraints.text: Team-season H2-H1 opponent change is likely low-reliability; SF-APPS-085 found ICC about 0.22 for an analogous player-level metric.
120 team-seasons may be too few to separate a stable trait from noise in an ICC or cross-season correlation.
Derived play-type and possession labels built from the same play-by-play as the outcome can leak outcome information, as in SF-APPS-068.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study tests a defense's opponent H2-H1 change as a reliable team trait. Analogous reliability (SF-APPS-085) and leakage/artifact studies (SF-APPS-068, SF15) bear on the method but do not answer the question. FAM:SF-APPS-018 is about counter-option ranking and is not cited as an answer.

risks.text: Split-half and cross-season reliability of team-season H2-H1 opponent change may be low; the analogous metric in SF-APPS-085 had ICC about 0.22.
120 team-seasons provide limited precision for an ICC or persistence estimate.
If defensive labels are built from the outcome period (second half), the H2 measure leaks into the reliability estimate (SF-APPS-068 pattern).
Pace, rotation, garbage time and score margin can drive H2-H1 change independently of defensive quality (SF15 pattern of composition confounding).
Play-type or possession labels derived from points scored can encode the outcome being predicted.
Rule, pace and roster changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may make team-seasons non-comparable across years (SF-APPS-018 flagged drift).
Scanning several H2-H1 windows, halves and defensive metrics raises false positives on reliability.
If most team-seasons show near-zero H2-H1 effect, a small true trait may be hard to detect (SF15 base-rate pattern).

design.estimand: Not proceeding as posed. Minimum viable test: the split-half or cross-season intraclass correlation of a defense's opponent H2-H1 PPP change, with CI, and the same estimate after Spearman-Brown adjustment.
design.unit: Team-season defense (opponent possessions faced by the team).
design.sample: 120 team-seasons across 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons; playoffs excluded in the minimum test. 2025-26 regular season used only after completion (from 2026-04-13).
design.power: Not computed. Before any run, simulate the CI width for ICC and Spearman-Brown estimates at 120 units and set a minimum detectable reliability; if the CI cannot exclude a low value, report untestable.
design.controls: Adjust for possessions per half, pace, score margin and garbage-time minutes; use defensive matchup minutes and rotation intervals to handle lineup changes; compute H2-H1 from fixed possession windows; exclude free-throw-only possessions as in SF15.
design.falsification: A reliability estimate whose CI includes the null of zero or a value below the pre-set threshold counts as failure; a placebo built from random halves must return reliability near zero.
design.multiplicity: One primary reliability estimate pre-registered; secondary windows and metrics labelled exploratory with correction.
design.decision_rule: Reliable trait is supported only if the lower CI bound of the primary ICC exceeds a pre-set threshold (for example 0.4) and the placebo estimate is near zero; otherwise report untestable or uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, with the 2025-26 season frozen after 2026-04-13; derived play-type graph records used only if their build excludes outcome-period points.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
